posts.idea: Anatomy of a card holder: a labelled carousel of the creator's own piece, laid flat on the bench
The two numbers: stitch spacing and total stitch count in one wallet
Five tools, not the kit: one tool per slide in the patent-print style
One edge fix in 'use X if you want Y' form, with a 'without the fix' frame
Patent-print style drawing of the card-holder pattern pieces, captioned 'Card holder, No. 07, 2026'

promised_sections.note: Thin, forum-based signals, but usable: the kit argument, edges as the quality marker, and the warning that #handstitched belongs to embroidery.
Says it is left empty on purpose and that the craft could not be seen. It gives only unverified account names and shop pages.
Four patterns borrowed from other crafts and adapted, with slide structures.
A term table with a basis for each term; no volumes.
Four ranked picks, each with a 'what would make it fail' note.
Neutral list of sources it could not reach.
Neutral list of what it inferred rather than observed.

price_why: Two posts are ready to shoot today and serve both beginners and buyers. The tag warning and the edge-fix angle are also worth having. The empty section and the scraping caveats mean it isn't a full $49 content plan.
one_line: A research brief for a hand-stitching leatherworker that borrows patterns from other crafts, adapts them into four ranked carousel ideas, and openly says what it could not see.
strongest: The 'Anatomy of a card holder' carousel. It uses the creator's own piece to teach beginners the vocabulary and to show buyers what to look for, with slides already specified.
weakest: A lot of the brief goes on method caveats, unreachable sources and a deliberately empty section. Several ideas also leave the format or the hook open.
